}}There are 496 cities in [[India]] with a population of over 100,000, of which 46 cities have a population of over 1,000,000. [[Mumbai]] is the most populated city followed by [[Delhi]], [[Bengaluru]] and [[Hyderabad]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=List of Most Populated cities in India |url=https://www.census2011.co.in/city.php |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=www.census2011.co.in}}</ref>

Cities are a type of [[Local government in India|sub-administrative unit]] and are defined by the [[Ministry of Home Affairs (India)|Ministry of Home Affairs]]. In some cases, cities are bifurcated into [[Municipal governance in India|municipalities]], which can lead to cities being included within other cities. This list is based on the [[Census of India]] using data from the [[2001 census of India]] and the [[2011 census of India]].

*The list is based on population within the boundaries of the respective Municipal Corporations and not the actual urban area.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|title=Provisional Population Totals Urban Agglomerations and Cities|url=http://censusindia.gov.in/2011-prov-results/paper2/data_files/India2/1.%20Data%20Highlight.pdf|website=Census of India 2011|access-date=30 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210418102638/https://censusindia.gov.in/2011-prov-results/paper2/data_files/India2/1.%20Data%20Highlight.pdf|archive-date=2021-04-18}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=City definition by census India |url=http://censusindia.gov.in/Metadata/Metada.htm#2c |publisher=censusindia.gov.in |access-date=26 May 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070617234445/http://www.censusindia.gov.in/Metadata/Metada.htm |archive-date=17 June 2007 }}</ref>
*Towns/Cities with populations of {{nowrap|1 [[lakh]]}} (100,000) are categorized as '''Class-I towns''' or '''Cities'''.
*The 46 cities with populations of {{nowrap|1 million}} and above are known as '''Million Plus UA'''s (urban agglomerations) or '''Cities'''.
*The 3 [[urban agglomerations|UA]]s with populations of {{nowrap|10 million}} and above are known as '''Mega Cities'''.{{efn|The census defines the three as Greater Mumbai UA (18.4 million), Delhi UA (16.3 million) and Kolkata UA (14.1&nbsp;million).}}<ref name="auto" />

The cities listed in '''bold''' are the capitals of the respective [[states and territories of India|states and union territories]] and the national capital [[New Delhi]]. <!-- The cities listed in ''curved text'' are considered as Megacities by United Nations. -->
